title: Bound clipboard history bytes and keep large copies as files
head: f5f35814d4a5
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Do not prune copies until the async history write has actually succeeded
leads.consequence: If an existing large-text row is removed after its file is older than two minutes and FileView cannot save (for example insufficient space or permission), saveHistory() still launches pruning with only the new in-memory names. It deletes the old file while the old on-disk JSON still references it. On restart the row appears, but paste-file's -r check fails. This applies even if the FileView write is merely still running; a saveFailed signal is never used. Quickshell 0.3.0 additionally warns on failed QSaveFile.commit() without setting state.error, so relying solely on its saved signal would not prove persistence. Serialize/verify the write before invoking deletion; keep referenced files on any failed save.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus (opus/followup-1-prune-save-order.md) confirmed with headless Quickshell 0.3.1 FileView run, low weight; published in Smaller notes

leads.summary: Normalize legacy history before using on-disk indices in the text paste helper
leads.consequence: A valid pre-upgrade array containing a >2 MiB text entry followed by a short entry passes load-history.sh, but parseHistory drops the first row and displays the short one with historyIndex 0. Until the next successful save, paste/copy of that displayed row calls the text helper, which reads index 0 from the original JSON and copies the oversized entry instead. A subsequent save fixes the index but permanently drops the older entry. Persist normalization before enabling indexed actions, or hand the selected text to the helper without indexing the unnormalized file.

leads.summary: Reject multiple JSON documents rather than silently disabling history writes
leads.consequence: The input '[{"type":"text","text":"hi"}]\n[]\n' contains two syntactically valid arrays. jq -e checks each and exits zero on the final true, so load-history.sh prints both documents and does not rename the rejected input. QML then calls JSON.parse on their concatenation, gets null, sets historyWritable=false, starts the watchers anyway, and silently discards saving on later captures until the user fixes the file and reloads. Check exactly one top-level JSON document, and return nonzero or rename aside if it fails the JS parser.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F5 (concatenated arrays); published in Smaller notes

leads.summary: Large-text UTF-16 heuristic drops NUL bytes that the small-copy decoder preserves
leads.consequence: For text/plain bytes consisting of 0x01 0x00 repetitions, the original Perl decoder detects control code points and falls back to the UTF-8 bytes, but the new large-copy sample classifies them as UTF-16LE and converts without the control-code guard. With ENTRY_LIMIT=16, 18 bytes become a 9-byte saved file with every NUL lost. With defaults the same pattern larger than 2 MiB follows the same path, and pasting the saved largetext cannot restore the original copy. Apply the small decoder's control-code rejection (and odd-length handling) to streaming conversion before storing the file.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F7; published in Smaller notes

leads.summary: Bound the preliminary wl-paste --list-types call as well as the payload
leads.consequence: Every capture, including watched copies already supplied on stdin, first runs the unbounded `wl-paste --list-types`. The 10-second timeout only wraps the later payload reader. If querying the compositor for MIME types stalls, the watcher child never reaches read_copy, does not emit a skipped marker and holds up clipboard recording indefinitely. Related #9488 explicitly adds a timeout to this query, so retain its guard when reconciling. The existing new fixture stubs --list-types with an immediate response.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F6 (#9488 list-types timeout); published in Related PRs

leads.summary: Reconcile #7452 image GC with rejected histories before merging both
leads.consequence: If #7452's GC is integrated unchanged with this PR's reject-and-start-fresh behavior, an unreadable/oversized valid history is renamed to .rejected-* and a later save writes a new JSON lacking its old images. #7452's gc.sh reads only the new JSON and removes unreferenced image files older than ten minutes, while this PR guards *only large-text* pruning when a rejected file exists. That destroys images still referenced in the preserved rejected JSON. Resolve the conflicting saveHistory hunk with an image-GC rejected-history guard before merging; because the overlapping branches conflict, this is a conditional integration lead, not a proven deployed regression.
leads.triage: dropped: hypothesis conditional on unmerged conflicting #7452 GC; not confirmed

leads.summary: Reconcile #11701 Ctrl+Enter with file-backed text rows
leads.consequence: If #11701's typeSelected is kept unchanged when resolving the overlapping QML hunk, Ctrl+Enter on every new largetext row closes the overlay and calls paste-text --type --history-index, because largetext has nonempty fullText and is not an image. Its text-only jq predicate rejects largetext and exits before any keystroke. Route that row via the file helper (or explicitly disable typing with feedback). The QML three-way merge actually has conflict markers at merge-11701.result.qml:313-332, so the exact final behavior depends on resolution.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified #11701 typeSelected (pr-11701.diff:181-189) and paste-text line 38; Opus self-check CORRECT; published as conditional on merge resolution

leads.summary: Reconcile #10919 plugin action payload with file-backed text metadata
leads.consequence: #10919 promises extension actions the complete original clipboard entry. If its entryForAction is integrated unchanged, largetext is neither an image nor a file URI: action.text becomes only the 8 KiB preview plus size label, and action.path becomes empty. An extension that edits or saves the supplied value cannot access the original large text. Add largetext path/MIME/size to the action payload and define how actions read file-backed entries. The PRs overlap ClipboardHistory.js and Clipboard.qml, so this is a conditional merge lead.

leads.summary: Test both largetext paste and copy dispatch, not only row MIME
leads.consequence: Removing both new largetext conditions from QML's applySelected and copySelected leaves 98/98 clipboard tests green. Yet a largetext row then goes to paste-text --history-index, which rejects its type, and the picker closes without copying/pasting. Add an assertion for both dispatch branches or a QML/controller fixture that exercises both actions with a real largetext row.
leads.triage: partly overlaps Opus F4; coordinator verified no test references applySelected/copySelected/largetext dispatch; published as test note without the Sol mutation result

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** for new copies, the PR bounds clipboard data as described. Capture is limited in bytes and by the read deadline, copies over 2 MiB (up to 256 MiB) are stored as `clipboard-text/<sha256>.txt` with a preview, and the loader refuses symlinks, special files and oversized files without following or opening them, and renames invalid JSON aside. Saves wait for a successful load. `test/shell.d/clipboard-test.sh` passes at the head (98 ok) and on a local merge with current `quattro` (98 ok). Also verified:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `read_copy`: source over the limit / stalled / empty | skipped (status 141, size limit + 1) / skipped (124) / not recorded |
| Inline decoder for copies up to 2 MiB | body byte-identical to `quattro`'s `emit_text`; existing UTF-16 tests pass |
| Re-copy of an existing large copy | same path, mtime refreshed |
| `prune-text.sh` | deletes only regular 64-hex `.txt` files older than a minute that are not in the overlay's keep list, plus `clipboard.*` temp files older than 60 minutes; keeps symlinks, other names and fresh files |
| Invalid-JSON history | kept on disk (the base returned `[]` and the next save overwrote the file) |

Three issues remain at the edges the tests do not reach, mostly for histories that already exist.

### Existing histories: oversized entries are dropped, and pastes can use the wrong entry until the next save

`normalizeEntry` now returns `null` for inline text over 2 Mi UTF-16 units (`ClipboardHistory.js:43`, `:52`), and `parseHistory` skips it. Nothing converts it to a large copy. Picker rows then carry indexes into the shorter in-memory list, while `bin/omarchy-clipboard-paste-text` (line 38) and `bin/omarchy-clipboard-open` still read `.[$index]` from the unchanged file:

```text
file on disk (written by current code)     in memory after load     row index
[0] newest small                           [0] newest small          0
[1] 3 MiB text      -- dropped
[2] older small                            [1] older small           1  -> paste-text reads file[1]
[3] image                                  [2] image                 2
```

In an isolated run with stub `wl-copy`, `paste-text --copy-only --history-index 1` copied the 3,145,728-byte dropped entry instead of "older small". The mismatch lasts until the first save, which after a login usually means the first copy. That save then removes the oversized entry for good. The base comment says "Pasting reads the full entry back from history by index, so nothing is lost" (base `ClipboardHistory.js:163`), and the PR description says it keeps that promise.

Two related upgrade cases:
- A legacy file over the 32 MiB ceiling is renamed aside whole (`load-history.sh:37`) and the loader exits 0 with `[]`. The picker opens empty with no message, because QML warns only on a non-zero exit (`Clipboard.qml:288`).
- A legacy history over the 8 MiB budget loads truncated and is saved that way: twelve 1 MiB entries loaded as 7.

**Impact:** on upgrade, users with large existing entries lose them, can paste or copy the wrong entry until the next save, and can see their whole history disappear without explanation.

**Suggested change:** migrate at load by writing oversized inline entries out as `clipboard-text` files, or ship a one-time migration. At minimum, save right after a load that dropped entries so the file and in-memory indexes agree. For a legacy file over the ceiling, a streamed migration (for example with `jq --stream`, not tried here) could keep the small entries, and the picker could say that a history was set aside.

### Any rejected history permanently disables large-copy pruning

`prune-text.sh:20` exits before deleting anything while any `clipboard-history.json.rejected-*` file exists, and nothing ever removes those files. In a probe with a rejected file present, a 10-minute-old unreferenced large copy was kept. Rejection happens automatically, not only for crafted files:

- an empty or whitespace-only history file (`jq -e` exits 4 on no input, `load-history.sh:43`); the base treated it as an empty history;
- a symlinked history, including one a user pointed elsewhere (for example into tmpfs). The base read and wrote through the link; now the link is renamed aside and a regular file is written in its place;
- a legacy file over 32 MiB (previous finding), a directory, a FIFO, invalid JSON, or JSON that is not an array.

**Impact:** after any rejection, the 1 GiB large-copy budget no longer bounds disk use: `addEntry` still drops entries, but their files stay, so every later large copy of up to 256 MiB accumulates. "Delete entire clipboard history" no longer removes large-copy files either. The rejected file itself keeps old clipboard contents on disk, outside anything the picker can clear. The same growth happens while `load-history.sh` exits 3, since saves (and therefore prunes) never run while capture keeps writing large copies.

**Suggested change:** limit the guard to the file names the rejected history actually references, or let the guard expire. Since rejected files can be oversized, invalid or empty, a format-independent scan such as `grep -aoE '[0-9a-f]{64}\.txt'` over the file would find those names where a `jq` read could not. Treat a zero-length or whitespace-only file as `[]`, as the base did, and tell the user when a history was rejected.

### The byte budget evicts all older entries at the first one that does not fit

`addEntry` always keeps the newest entry and then stops at the first older entry that does not fit the 8 MiB budget (`break`, `ClipboardHistory.js:137`); `parseHistory` does the same (`:108`). One inline entry can be 2 Mi units, a quarter of the budget, and up to about six times that once control characters are JSON-escaped. Probe results:

- 400 small entries followed by four newline-rich copies of about 2 MiB each left 3 entries, none of them small.
- One control-heavy copy of 1.5 Mi characters (9 MiB serialized) left a history of 1.

**Impact:** a few ordinary copies just under the 2 MiB inline limit (a log, a JSON dump) permanently wipe the rest of the history, since the result is saved to disk. Copies over 2 MiB are not affected this way, because they go to files and add only a short preview to the budget.

**Suggested change:** large copies already use `continue` so small entries survive. Either skip rather than break for oversized inline entries, or lower the threshold for storing a copy as a file (for example to a few hundred KiB) so the budget holds many entries.

### Related open PRs

- **#9488** conflicts with this head in `capture.sh`: both change the one-shot `wl-paste --type text` line. It merges cleanly only with the first commit (`a157ae2`), so the description's "merge cleanly" is out of date for #9488. #9488 also adds a timeout to `wl-paste --list-types`, which this PR leaves unbounded (`capture.sh:35`) and which runs before every capture, watched ones included. A resolution could keep that timeout.
- **#10919:** keeping both sides is not enough. Its `entryForAction` builds `text: fullText(entry)` and sets `path` only for images and single `file://` entries, so for a `largetext` entry an extension gets the 8 KB preview plus "… N MB in all" and an empty path. It needs a `largetext` branch that passes the path and MIME type.
- **#11701:** its `typeSelected` sends every non-image row with non-empty `fullText` to `omarchy-clipboard-paste-text --type`. A `largetext` row has a preview as `fullText`, and `paste-text` accepts only `type == "text"` (line 38), so Ctrl+Enter on a large copy would close the picker and do nothing. The two PRs conflict in that QML hunk, so the outcome depends on the resolution.
- **Current `quattro`:** the PR conflicts only in `test/shell.d/clipboard-test.sh` (the Tensaku to Omasnap rename next to the appended tests). The resolved merge passes 98.

### Smaller notes

- **Prune runs before the save is known to have landed.** `saveHistory()` starts `prune-text.sh` right after `setText` (`Clipboard.qml:87-91`), which only starts an asynchronous write. If the write fails and the same save dropped a large copy, that file can be deleted (once it is about a minute old) while the old history still lists it. In headless Quickshell 0.3.1, a read-only history file and an unwritable directory emitted `saveFailed`, and a small failed write emitted `saved` after logging "Atomic commit failed". After a restart the row comes back, and pasting it silently does nothing (`omarchy-clipboard-paste-file` exits at its `-r` check). A bounded read of the on-disk history in `prune-text.sh`, keeping every large-copy name it lists and deleting nothing if it cannot be parsed, fixed this in a probe. Also running prune from `onSaved` would avoid deletions lagging one save behind, which matters for Clear, but `onSaved` alone misses the commit failure reported as `saved`.
- **Loader and parser disagree on valid JSON.** `jq -e` accepts two concatenated arrays and `[NaN]`, so `load-history.sh` passes them through, but `parseHistory` returns `null` for both. `historyWritable` then stays false with nothing logged, and the overlay stops saving in every session. A `console.warn` for a `null` parse, or handling it like the reject path, would make this visible.
- **Large-copy UTF-16 detection** lacks the inline decoder's check for control characters after decoding. Input of `01 00` pairs stays raw as an inline copy but is stored with the NUL bytes removed as a large copy.
- **`trap 'exit 143' TERM INT HUP` is redundant and delays exit.** Bash already runs the EXIT trap on terminating signals once one is set. With the explicit trap, `capture.sh` waited for the read to end (4.5 s after SIGTERM with a 5 s deadline). Without it, it exited at once, and both variants removed the temp file.
- **Removing `watchChanges`** means an outside edit or delete of the history file is no longer picked up, and the next save overwrites it. The base reloaded on change.

**Optional test improvement:** in a mutation run, each of these changes still passed all 98 tests: removing the loader's size ceiling or accepting non-array JSON; removing `prune-text.sh`'s rejected-history guard, its `-mmin +1` age check or its name filter; removing the re-copy `touch`; disabling large-copy UTF-16 conversion; removing the `historyWritable` guard or the prune call; and lowering `historyFileLimit` from 32 to 13 MiB. That last one passes because "clipboard never writes a history its loader would refuse" checks only the final state (one 12.6 MB entry), not the 23.6 MB state just before it. The test file also has no assertion on the `largetext` branches in `applySelected` and `copySelected`. Checking the file size after each `addEntry` would cover the file limit, and regex assertions for the QML guards (as this test file already uses for other QML properties) would cover those; the loader, prune and capture rules need their own shell cases.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the head, base and current `quattro`, plus upstream Quickshell 0.3.1, wl-clipboard 2.3.0, Qt and bash sources where conclusions depend on them. `clipboard-test.sh` and `qml-text-format-test.sh` were run in an isolated sandbox at the head and on a local merge with `quattro`, and `clipboard-test.sh` against mutated copies. Script and helper probes used stub `wl-paste`/`wl-copy`; headless Quickshell probes covered `FileView` saves and the load path. No overlay was launched, no live clipboard was used, the full `test/shell` suite was not run, the memory figures in the description were not re-measured, and timings come from the sandbox.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
